placers.name: Payton Carpenter
placers.note: Class of 2031: a seventh grader, 2nd at 100 in the 2026 AHSAA girls championship. Alabama lets seventh and eighth graders wrestle for a member school and the medal is real, but the platform mints a profile only for a current class year (2027-2030), so a class of 2031 has nowhere to sit and a guessed one would be worse. The placement is stored and linked; she gets a profile when 2031 enters the window. Class year from the grade the tournament published (28 Oct 2026).

placers.name: Wyteria Powe
placers.note: Class of 2031: a seventh grader, 3rd at 152 in the 2026 AHSAA girls championship. Same as Payton Carpenter - a real medal, a class year the current window does not reach. The placement is stored and linked; she gets a profile when 2031 enters it (28 Oct 2026).

placers.name: Katie Lowe
placers.note: Class year held blank, so no profile. The 2025 state champion at 152 and 4th in 2026, but the two Flo participant grades contradict each other - 2025 'HS Sophomore' reads 2027, 2026 'HS Senior' reads 2026 - and each is independently corroborated in print: AHSAA's own 2025 recap lists her 'So.' at 31-6, SEWrestle's 2026 Fan's Guide lists her 'Sr.' No RankWrestlers profile exists to break the tie. Held rather than guessed; detail in Muse's AL-IMPORT-NOTE.md (28 Oct 2026).

preFreshmanVerified.note: Peyton Andrews, Weaver, class of 2028. Before his freshman year he placed 6 in 2024. Alabama allows it: AHSAA feeder eligibility admits seventh and eighth graders, and the 2026 championship's own participant grades carry 164 eighth-grade and 27 seventh-grade slots. The class year comes from that published grade, which is the same field that flags the result as pre-freshman here. Different from Maryland (COMAR 13A.06.03.02, grades 9-12 only) and Virginia (VHSL 28-2-1, eighth graders on junior varsity only), where the same shape proved a class year wrong (28 Oct 2026).
